---
title: "PairLoom ≤200 s full-sample merge at 4 workers — optimization plan"
author: "Yun Jiang"
date: today
---

# Objective

Process the GO00009 S19 full dataset (6.08M prep-surviving templates) in
≤200 s wall on this machine with `--threads 4`, rescue enabled, with
outputs and biological decisions preserved exactly: identical merged and
unmerged BAM records (SEQ/QUAL/CIGAR/MAPQ/tags), identical disagreement
parquet content, identical read-stats classifications, and a byte-identical
done line (statistical counts). Current baseline: 1,938 s full / 31.3 s
pilot (99,401 templates) — a ~9.7x speedup is required.

# Ordered approach (per the user's instruction)

1. Reduce per-base observation transport: workers currently ship 15.2M
   `OverlapObservation` objects per 100k pairs across the process boundary
   and the main process re-aggregates one call per base. Pre-aggregate per
   chunk in the worker and bulk-merge compact entries in the main process.
2. Reduce repeated reference searches: memoize rescue whole-reference
   uniqueness scans by searched block; keep a per-worker concatenated
   reference blob for scans; audit the ReferenceCache (4-contig LRU against
   a 21,839-contig panel) for thrash on the rescue path.
3. Reduce SAM serialization: replace the SAM-string round-trips on the
   parallel path (`to_string` -> pickle -> `fromstring` -> process ->
   `to_string` -> `fromstring`) with pysam binary record transport
   (`to_binary`/`from_binary`), keeping the single-process path direct.
4. Benchmark each change on the pilot (defaults, `--threads 4`, GNU time,
   no profiler) and keep only wins; require the equivalence gate after
   every kept change.
5. If Python execution remains the bottleneck (expected: `try_merge`'s
   per-position consensus loop and `build_read_structure`'s per-base dict
   construction are ~50% of profiled time), implement a batched Rust core
   (pyo3, built into the pixi env) covering structure building, the merge
   loop, and overlap-observation aggregation — not a package rewrite. Port
   semantics exactly; the Python pipeline keeps orchestration, rescue
   placement policy, record construction, and output ordering.

# Equivalence gate (after every stage)

1. Snapshot the current implementation as the baseline (PYTHONPATH override
   copy); run baseline and optimized on `data/pilot/B.aln.bam` (defaults,
   4 threads).
2. Compare: per-record SAM-string equality on merged and unmerged BAMs in
   stream order; parquet frame equality (disagreement + read-stats); done
   line byte equality; full test suite green (182).
3. Only after the pilot gate passes: one full-dataset run, timed, with the
   same equivalence comparisons against the baseline full outputs.

# Files

- `src/pairloom/{pipeline,merge,overlap,alignment,parquetout,rescue,reference}.py`
- new `rust/` crate + pixi build wiring, if Phase 5 is reached
- `benchmarks/equivalence_check.py` (baseline-vs-candidate comparison)
- README performance section update on success

# Risks

- pysam binary transport API availability in 0.24.1 — verify before
  relying on it; fall back to passing objects via fork-inherited state or
  keeping strings only where cheap.
- Byte-identical outputs across process counts depend on unchanged template
  order and record content; the parallel drain order must stay strict.
- Parquet determinism: same pyarrow version, same batch settings, else
  compare frames not bytes.
- Rust build must live inside the pixi env reproducibly (rust + maturin
  deps); the gate is the suite + equivalence, not the profiler.
- Editable install shadows: baseline snapshot must be imported via
  PYTHONPATH precedence, verified before benchmarking.

# Verification

1. Pilot: time (GNU time, no profiler) after each change; equivalence gate
   green after each kept change.
2. Suite: `pixi run test` 182 passed, lint/format clean.
3. Full dataset: ≤200 s at 4 threads with rescue on; equivalence gate green
   against baseline full outputs; report timing table.
